tasks.question: Choose a cache eviction approach for an offline editor. Compare bounded LRU with segmented LRU under the supplied limits; separate RAM cost, disk persistence and assumptions.

evidence.text: Cache budget: 48 decimal MB. Interactive documents require at most 16 MB; background indexing can request 40 MB. Cache entries are reconstructible. Saved user documents must survive restart. No latency measurements exist.

tasks.question: Explain which users may edit an archived project according to these excerpts. Identify any unresolved conflict without inventing an override rule.

evidence.text: Project editors may change active projects. Archived projects are read-only unless an owner reopens them.

tasks.question: Compare two batch strategies under the given assumptions. Calculate their stated throughput and discuss whether that alone establishes interactive latency.

evidence.text: Hypothetical batch A processes 12 items in 0.4 seconds; batch B processes 24 items in 0.6 seconds. Arrival pattern, waiting time and per-item latency distribution are unknown. No benchmark was executed.

tasks.question: Recommend a delivery sequence that fits the team budget. Explain dependencies, parallel work and missing estimates rather than assume unlimited people.

evidence.text: One engineer has 30 hours available this week. Task A requires 8 hours. B requires 12 hours after A. C requires 8 hours and can start immediately. Release review requires 4 hours after B and C. All durations are estimates; no outsourcing or additional payment is allowed.
